PRIORITY BUILD (owner: "the SG2 meta is supposed to be in the kernel — not having it there is a cut corner"): port SuperGrok2's full meta-net into the PERSISTENT MEGAKERNEL as in-kernel stages in /workspace/SuperGrok1.5 (branch claude/h100-audit-maximal). NO builds, NO GPU runs (validation gates own the GPU). Owner directives: no functionality suppressed (EVERY mechanism live in-kernel); no CUDA graphs; components portable per csrc/fused/COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md (read it first).

WHAT EXISTS (read these as your sources of truth):
- The COMPLETE SG2 meta math as separate per-launch kernels: grokking_optimizers/kernels/sm_90/supergrok2_sm90.cuh — csa_hca_step_one orchestrates ~15-20 kernel launches per step: input projection + |grad|-sort → CSA (compress-KV, indexer-Q/K, top-k, windowed online-softmax attention) → HCA (stride-dense attention) → per-element matrix-GRU → PEER product-key routing + experts → sg2_apply_kernel (smart_grad = g + alpha·mu_new + lamb_eff·slow_new, then Adam tail). All math is already written as device code; your job is RESTRUCTURING the launches into stages of ONE persistent kernel.
- The persistent substrate + a PROVEN reference implementation of exactly this restructuring: csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh (real decoder fwd+bwd as stages: gridDim=#SMs, 256 thr/CTA, work partitioned per CTA, grid barriers between stages via megakernel_common.cuh PersistentContext, deterministic reductions, apply_optimizer tail). Mirror its structure, barrier discipline, and validation methodology.
- Canonical apply math: csrc/algorithms/supergrok2.h (sg2_apply_step — just rebuilt+parity-passed 13/0; do NOT modify it, CALL it).
- The meta weight bundle is SMALL (d_model=8, gru_hidden=4, 144 experts × 16 hidden, pk_dim etc. — read the dims from grokking_optimizers/optimizers/supergrok2.py constructor defaults + OPTIMIZER_CONFIGS["supergrok2"] in grokking_race_v2.py): it fits in shared memory — stage it once per kernel, zero re-reads from HBM across stages.

DESIGN REQUIREMENTS:
1. New header csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh (per the portability contract: self-contained, includes only the substrate + algorithms headers + CUDA; no globals; documented stage contract). Implement `sg2_meta_stages<Dims>`: the full pipeline over the flat gradient vector (n elements), CTAs partitioning the element/sequence space, ONE grid barrier between stages that have cross-CTA dependencies (the sort and the attention windows are the couplings — study how the existing kernels partition: the sort is global (which sort does it use? read sg2_input_proj_sort_kernel — if it's a global bitonic/radix over n, that's a multi-pass stage with barriers; transcribe its passes as barrier-separated stage iterations), attention windows/topk are sequence-local after sort, GRU + PEER + apply are element-local). Every mechanism stays EXACTLY as the per-launch math computes it — your deliverable is launch-elimination, not math change. Deterministic: no float atomics (the per-launch kernels' reductions — check each; replace any cross-CTA float atomic with the deterministic owner-computes pattern proven in F3's MoE-bwd rework and the decoder cell's reduce).
2. A new cell csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_decoder_real_supergrok2.cu? NO — scope: the OPTIMIZER stage must compose with ANY model stage. Build it as the optimizer half consumed by launch_fused_megakernel-style composition: provide `launch_sg2_meta_optimizer_tail(PersistentContext, grads, params, all state ptrs incl mu/slow/gru, the smem-staged weight bundle ptrs, FusedScalars, stream)` — a standalone persistent kernel for the OPTIMIZER STEP ONLY (consumes the real grad the model bwd produced — the L1-style contract agent A established, but now SG2's FULL meta runs inside one persistent kernel instead of ~20 launches). Integration with the model-fused L3 cells is the integrator's job — leave a precise INTEGRATION-NOTES.md section (what the combined cell must wire).
3. Python driver: extend the pattern in grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py?? NO — dispatch.py is shared; instead write the driver as a documented function in your new header's companion test + an INTEGRATION-NOTES.md at repo root (what binding signature the integrator must add to bindings.cpp: you may NOT touch bindings.cpp — sibling agent territory). Deliver the .cu/.cuh + the exact m.def signature spec + the python call-shape.
4. VALIDATION (the decoder methodology, mandatory): (a) a single-threaded PYTHON MIRROR of your staged pipeline (tests/hw/sg2_kernel_mirror.py) matched against the EXISTING eager path outputs — drive supergrok2.py's cached-weights kernel-ABI view on CPU... the existing Python reference is _single_param_step + the meta_net forward; build the mirror to match the KERNEL pipeline structure (sort order, window membership, topk ties, GRU order) and assert agreement with a direct reimplementation oracle to ~1e-12 (fp64), exactly like tests/hw/decoder_kernel_mirror.py did (read it as the template — it caught a real aliasing bug pre-CUDA). (b) GPU-gated test spec added to tests/hw/test_megakernel_vs_eager.py is the INTEGRATOR's job — instead put the test in a NEW file tests/hw/test_sg2_megakernel.py (you own it): single-step parity vs the existing csa_hca_step_one path (same inputs → smart_grad/moments/params within 1e-5; the existing path is the oracle since it's parity-validated), plus a 200-step trajectory check. Mark hw-gated.
5. Honesty rails: no placeholder math; if a sub-mechanism cannot be staged in this pass (e.g., the global sort proves architecturally hostile), DO NOT fake it — implement the launch-free version of everything else and leave the sort as ONE explicit pre-kernel launch with a loud header comment quantifying the residual (e.g., "1 sort launch + 1 persistent kernel vs the previous ~20 launches") and the path to eliminating it. State this in the report. The bar is maximal honest launch-elimination with bit-faithful math.
6. bf16 note: compute precision fp32 in this pass (matches the parity-validated apply); leave a flagged bf16-compute TODO consistent with the decoder cell's.
Report: stage/barrier layout, smem budget, sort handling, determinism approach, the mirror/oracle agreement numbers, integration spec for the binding, and the launch-count before/after.

1	# Fused-megakernel component contract (portability spec)
2	
3	Owner requirement (2026-06-09): every (model × optimizer × arch) configuration —
4	all 3 models × 11 optimizers — composes into ONE persistent megakernel binary,
5	and the building blocks are **individually portable**: a third project lifts the
6	headers and instantiates a fused trainer without dragging this repo along. The
7	meta-programming lives in headers; the dispatch layer is generated and is the
8	only composition seam.
9	
10	## Component taxonomy (header-only, self-contained)
11	
12	| component | header(s) | contract |
13	|---|---|---|
14	| **Substrate** | `csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh` | `PersistentContext` (task counter, grid barrier, generation), one-CTA-per-SM persistent launch idiom. Depends on CUDA runtime only. |
15	| **Optimizer math** | `csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h` (×11) | Pure per-element apply math (`<opt>_step(...)`), no CUDA dependencies beyond `__device__` qualifiers, no state allocation, no I/O. Single source of truth — everything else `#include`s these (enforced by `scripts/check_math_single_source.py`). Already portable as-is. |
16	| **Optimizer tails** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh` | `apply_optimizer<OptId>(FusedOptState&, FusedScalars const&, ...)` — templates composing the algorithm headers into megakernel stages. Consumes the documented POD structs only. |
17	| **Model stages** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_<model>.cuh` (decoder / vit / mamba3 — ONE HEADER PER MODEL, not a monolith) | Provides `model_<m>_forward_stage<Dims>` and `model_<m>_backward_stage<Dims>`: batch-slice-local fwd/bwd with all activations CTA-local, writing per-CTA weight-grad partials to a caller-provided workspace. Templated on compile-time dims (d_model, n_layers, n_heads, seq, vocab). Includes ONLY the substrate header + CUDA. No globals, no repo build flags (every `SG_TUNED_*` consumed via `#ifndef` defaults). |
18	| **Composition** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_megakernel.cuh` | `launch_fused_megakernel<ModelId, OptId, Tier>` — stage pipeline: fwd → bwd → grid barrier → deterministic weight-grad reduction → optimizer tail. The only place stages and tails meet. |
19	| **Cells** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_<model>_<opt>.cu` (×33) | GENERATED 36-line instantiations (`megakernel_codegen.py`). Never hand-edited. |
20	| **Dispatch** | `csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp` + generated `fused_wired_cells.inc` / `fused_dispatch_table.inc` | `(model, optimizer, arch) → cell` routing. Generated from the same enumeration as the cells, so it cannot drift. Loud-gated: unwired/unready cells throw, never silently degrade. |
21	
22	## Portability rules (apply to every new/edited component)
23	1. **Self-containment**: a component header compiles with `#include <cuda_runtime.h>`
24	   + its declared includes only. Include-what-you-use; no transitive reliance.
25	2. **No hidden state**: no globals, no statics with side effects; all state flows
26	   through the documented POD structs (`PersistentContext`, `FusedOptState`,
27	   `FusedScalars`) or explicit pointers.
28	3. **Compile-time configuration only via documented template params or
29	   `#ifndef`-defaulted macros** (`SG_TUNED_*`); absent definitions must yield a
30	   correct (if untuned) kernel.
31	4. **The lift test**: copying `megakernel_common.cuh` + one `model_stage_*.cuh`
32	   + `opt_components.cuh` + the relevant `csrc/algorithms/*.h` into a fresh
33	   project and instantiating `launch_fused_megakernel<M,O,Tier>` must build and
34	   run. Each phase's validation includes compiling a minimal out-of-tree TU
35	   (tests/hw/test_component_portability.cu) that includes ONLY those headers.
36	5. **Generated artifacts are never edited by hand** — change the generator,
37	   regenerate everything, `git diff` must be generator-consistent.
38	6. **No placeholder math** on any wired path (owner no-suppression directive);
39	   surrogate stages exist only behind explicit unreadiness gates and throw at
40	   dispatch.
41	
42	## Phase status
43	- Phase 1 (in flight): real decoder fwd+bwd stages, validated vs eager — lands
44	  in `model_stages.cuh`, then is split per-model per this contract.
45	- Phase 2: vit + mamba3 stage headers (built against this contract natively).
46	- Phase 3: optimizer precompute stages in-kernel for the 9 non-trivial tails;
47	  SuperGrok2's CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta as in-kernel stages (the full
48	  "vit×sg2 in one binary").

166	// ── (1) CSA / HCA KV compression ─────────────────────────────────────────
167	//  Projects the sorted feature sequence through a weight matrix, then pools
168	//  the projected sequence into compressed K (or V) entries. We fuse the two
169	//  steps per output (j, d): pool the *raw* features then project, which is
170	//  equivalent for a linear projection (Σ_w a_w (W x_t) = W (Σ_w a_w x_t)).
171	//  Grid: one thread per (compressed-entry j, channel d). proj_W is row-major
172	//  [d_model, d_model]; out[j, d] = Σ_k proj_W[d,k] * pooled[k].
173	
174	template <typename feat_t, typename wt_t = float>
175	__global__ void csa_compress_kv_kernel(
176	    const feat_t* __restrict__ x_seq,        // [N, d_model] sorted features
177	    const wt_t*   __restrict__ proj_W,       // [d_model, d_model] K or V proj
178	    const float*  __restrict__ compress_logits, // [csa_window] pooling logits
179	    float* __restrict__ c_out,               // [Nc, d_model] compressed K/V
180	    int N, int d_model, int Nc,
181	    int csa_compress, int csa_window
182	) {
183	    const int total = Nc * d_model;
184	    const int stride = gridDim.x * blockDim.x;
185	    for (int idx = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; idx < total; idx += stride) {
186	        const int j = idx / d_model;   // compressed-entry index
187	        const int d = idx % d_model;   // output channel
188	        float acc = 0.0f;
189	        #pragma unroll 4
190	        for (int k = 0; k < d_model; k++) {
191	            // pooled[k] for this compressed entry
192	            const float pooled = alg::sg2_csa_compress_kv<feat_t>(
193	                x_seq, compress_logits, j, k, N, d_model, csa_compress, csa_window);
194	            acc += static_cast<float>(proj_W[d * d_model + k]) * pooled;
195	        }
196	        c_out[j * d_model + d] = acc;
197	    }
198	}

200	template <typename feat_t, typename wt_t = float>
201	__global__ void hca_compress_kv_kernel(
202	    const feat_t* __restrict__ x_seq,        // [N, d_model] sorted features
203	    const wt_t*   __restrict__ proj_W,       // [d_model, d_model] K or V proj
204	    const float*  __restrict__ hca_w,        // [hca_compress] weights, or nullptr (mean)
205	    float* __restrict__ c_out,               // [Nh, d_model] compressed K/V
206	    int N, int d_model, int Nh,
207	    int hca_compress
208	) {
209	    const int total = Nh * d_model;
210	    const int stride = gridDim.x * blockDim.x;
211	    for (int idx = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; idx < total; idx += stride) {
212	        const int j = idx / d_model;
213	        const int d = idx % d_model;
214	        float acc = 0.0f;
215	        #pragma unroll 4
216	        for (int k = 0; k < d_model; k++) {
217	            const float pooled = alg::sg2_hca_compress_kv<feat_t>(
218	                x_seq, hca_w, j, k, N, d_model, hca_compress);
219	            acc += static_cast<float>(proj_W[d * d_model + k]) * pooled;
220	        }
221	        c_out[j * d_model + d] = acc;
222	    }
223	}

225	// ── (1b) Query projection ────────────────────────────────────────────────
226	//  q[t, d] = Σ_k q_W[d,k] * x_seq[t,k].  Grid over (t, d).
227	
228	template <typename feat_t, typename wt_t = float>
229	__global__ void project_q_kernel(
230	    const feat_t* __restrict__ x_seq,        // [N, d_model]
231	    const wt_t*   __restrict__ q_W,          // [d_model, d_model]
232	    float* __restrict__ q_out,               // [N, d_model]
233	    int N, int d_model
234	) {
235	    const int total = N * d_model;
236	    const int stride = gridDim.x * blockDim.x;
237	    for (int idx = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; idx < total; idx += stride) {
238	        const int t = idx / d_model;
239	        const int d = idx % d_model;
240	        float acc = 0.0f;
241	        #pragma unroll 4
242	        for (int k = 0; k < d_model; k++)
243	            acc += static_cast<float>(q_W[d * d_model + k])
244	                 * static_cast<float>(x_seq[t * d_model + k]);
245	        q_out[idx] = acc;
246	    }
247	}

249	// ── (1c) Indexer projections ─────────────────────────────────────────────
250	//  qI[t] = (x[t] @ idx_DQ) @ idx_UQ  ... but spec uses qI directly as a
251	//  rank-`indexer_rank` vector; we compute the low-rank query qI[t,r] =
252	//  Σ_k (Σ_m x[t,m] idx_DQ[m,r']) — here idx_DQ is [d_model, rank] so
253	//  qI[t,r] = Σ_m x[t,m] * idx_DQ[m,r]. The UQ up-projection is folded into
254	//  the key side equivalently; we keep the rank-space dot product (spec §2:
255	//  I = qI·kI / sqrt(rank)). kI[s,r] = Σ_m c_pooled[s,m] * idx_K[m,r].
256	
257	template <typename feat_t, typename wt_t = float>
258	__global__ void indexer_q_kernel(
259	    const feat_t* __restrict__ x_seq,        // [N, d_model]
260	    const wt_t*   __restrict__ idx_DQ,       // [d_model, rank]
261	    float* __restrict__ qI_out,              // [N, rank]
262	    int N, int d_model, int rank
263	) {
264	    const int total = N * rank;
265	    const int stride = gridDim.x * blockDim.x;
266	    for (int idx = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; idx < total; idx += stride) {
267	        const int t = idx / rank;
268	        const int r = idx % rank;
269	        float acc = 0.0f;
270	        #pragma unroll 4
271	        for (int m = 0; m < d_model; m++)
272	            acc += static_cast<float>(x_seq[t * d_model + m])
273	                 * static_cast<float>(idx_DQ[m * rank + r]);
274	        qI_out[idx] = acc;
275	    }
276	}
277	
278	template <typename feat_t, typename wt_t = float>
279	__global__ void indexer_k_kernel(
280	    const feat_t* __restrict__ x_seq,        // [N, d_model] (compressed pool source)
281	    const wt_t*   __restrict__ idx_K,        // [d_model, rank]
282	    const float*  __restrict__ compress_logits, // [csa_window]
283	    float* __restrict__ kI_out,              // [Nc, rank]
284	    int N, int d_model, int Nc, int rank,
285	    int csa_compress, int csa_window
286	) {
287	    const int total = Nc * rank;
288	    const int stride = gridDim.x * blockDim.x;
289	    for (int idx = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; idx < total; idx += stride) {
290	        const int s = idx / rank;
291	        const int r = idx % rank;
292	        float acc = 0.0f;
293	        #pragma unroll 4
294	        for (int m = 0; m < d_model; m++) {
295	            const float pooled = alg::sg2_csa_compress_kv<feat_t>(
296	                x_seq, compress_logits, s, m, N, d_model, csa_compress, csa_window);
297	            acc += pooled * static_cast<float>(idx_K[m * rank + r]);
298	        }
299	        kI_out[idx] = acc;
300	    }
301	}

303	// ── (2) CSA indexer top-k selection ──────────────────────────────────────
304	//  For each query t, score all Nc compressed entries with the lightning
305	//  indexer and select the top-k by insertion into a small local array.
306	//  Writes the selected compressed-entry indices into sel_idx[t, 0..topk-1]
307	//  (padded with -1 when topk > Nc).
308	
309	__global__ void csa_indexer_topk_kernel(
310	    const float* __restrict__ qI,            // [N, rank]
311	    const float* __restrict__ kI,            // [Nc, rank]
312	    int* __restrict__ sel_idx,               // [N, topk]
313	    int N, int Nc, int rank, int topk
314	) {
315	    const int t = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
316	
317	    // SMEM-staged top-k scratch: the best_score[CSA_MAX_TOPK] /
318	    // best_idx[CSA_MAX_TOPK] buffers were a 128-slot per-thread register array
319	    // (the dominant register cost of this kernel and a guaranteed local-memory
320	    // spill on real ptxas). Relocating them into this thread's private slice of
321	    // dynamic shared is BIT-IDENTICAL: the insertion-sort reads/writes and the
322	    // final sel_idx stores are unchanged in value and order. Layout:
323	    // [blockDim.x * CSA_MAX_TOPK] floats then [blockDim.x * CSA_MAX_TOPK] ints.
324	    extern __shared__ float topk_smem[];
325	    float* best_score = topk_smem + threadIdx.x * CSA_MAX_TOPK;
326	    int*   best_idx   = reinterpret_cast<int*>(
327	                            topk_smem + blockDim.x * CSA_MAX_TOPK)
328	                        + threadIdx.x * CSA_MAX_TOPK;
329	    if (t >= N) return;
330	
331	    const int K = min(topk, CSA_MAX_TOPK);
332	    #pragma unroll
333	    for (int i = 0; i < CSA_MAX_TOPK; i++) { best_score[i] = -INFINITY; best_idx[i] = -1; }
334	
335	    const float* q = qI + t * rank;
336	    for (int s = 0; s < Nc; s++) {
337	        const float sc = alg::sg2_csa_index_score(q, kI + s * rank, rank);
338	        // Insertion into the sorted (descending) top-K buffer.
339	        if (sc > best_score[K - 1]) {
340	            int p = K - 1;
341	            while (p > 0 && best_score[p - 1] < sc) {
342	                best_score[p] = best_score[p - 1];
343	                best_idx[p]   = best_idx[p - 1];
344	                p--;
345	            }
346	            best_score[p] = sc;
347	            best_idx[p]   = s;
348	        }
349	    }
350	    for (int i = 0; i < K; i++) sel_idx[t * topk + i] = best_idx[i];
351	}

353	// §4.2 cp.async query staging helper (shared by CSA + HCA attention).
354	//
355	//  Both attention kernels read the per-thread query vector qv[0..head_dim)
356	//  REPEATEDLY (once per top-k entry and once per window token). That makes the
357	//  query the reused global->shared staging load — the prime cp.async target.
358	//  Each thread stages its own head_dim-float query slice into its private slot
359	//  qsh[threadIdx.x*head_dim .. +head_dim) with hand-issued cp.async.ca (4B)
360	//  copies, split into `kCsaAsyncDepth` groups kept in flight so the query-load
361	//  latency overlaps the first key's address math. After cp_async_wait_all the
362	//  staged slice is BYTE-IDENTICAL to a synchronous load of qv (no numeric
363	//  change). The streaming K/V reads stay direct (read once, no reuse benefit).
364	//
365	//  NOTE: these kernels are 1-thread-per-(query,head) with no __syncthreads, so
366	//  each thread waits only on ITS OWN cp.async groups — no block-wide barrier
367	//  is needed (and none exists) to make the private slot visible to the owner.
368	__device__ __forceinline__ const float* csa_stage_query_async(
369	    float* qsh,              // dynamic shared: [blockDim.x * head_dim]
370	    const float* __restrict__ qv_global,  // [head_dim] this thread's query
371	    int head_dim
372	) {
373	    float* qslot = qsh + threadIdx.x * head_dim;
374	    // Split head_dim into kCsaAsyncDepth roughly-equal chunks; commit each as
375	    // its own group so up to kCsaAsyncDepth copies are in flight at once.
376	    const int chunk = (head_dim + kCsaAsyncDepth - 1) / kCsaAsyncDepth;
377	    #pragma unroll
378	    for (int g = 0; g < kCsaAsyncDepth; ++g) {
379	        const int e0 = g * chunk;
380	        const int e1 = (e0 + chunk < head_dim) ? (e0 + chunk) : head_dim;
381	        for (int e = e0; e < e1; ++e) {
382	            prim::cp_async_ca_4(&qslot[e], &qv_global[e]);
383	        }
384	        prim::cp_async_commit();
385	    }
386	    prim::cp_async_wait_all();  // drain all groups: qslot now == qv (byte-exact)
387	    return qslot;
388	}

390	// ── (3) CSA attention ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
391	//  Per query t and head h: online-softmax attention over the selected
392	//  top-k compressed entries ∪ the causal sliding window (last csa_window raw
393	//  tokens, i.e. positions [t-csa_window+1 .. t]). Multi-query: K/V shared
394	//  across heads (compressed K/V are [Nc, d_model]; raw-window K/V reuse the
395	//  same q/k/v projections — here the window keys/values are the compressed
396	//  projections of single raw tokens). Output csa_ctx[t] passes through out_W.
397	//  Grid: one thread per (query t, head h).
398	
399	__global__ void csa_attention_kernel(
400	    const float* __restrict__ q,             // [N, d_model] projected queries
401	    const float* __restrict__ c_k,           // [Nc, d_model] compressed keys
402	    const float* __restrict__ c_v,           // [Nc, d_model] compressed values
403	    const float* __restrict__ win_k,         // [N, d_model] per-token window keys
404	    const float* __restrict__ win_v,         // [N, d_model] per-token window values
405	    const int*   __restrict__ sel_idx,       // [N, topk] selected compressed entries
406	    const float* __restrict__ out_W,         // [d_model, d_model]
407	    float* __restrict__ csa_ctx,             // [N, d_model] output
408	    int N, int Nc, int d_model, int num_heads,
409	    int head_dim, int topk, int csa_window
410	) {
411	    const int gid = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
412	    const int total = N * num_heads;
413	    // §4.2 cp.async query staging buffer + SMEM-staged online-softmax
414	    // accumulator. Layout: [blockDim.x * head_dim] query slots, then
415	    // [blockDim.x * head_dim] accumulator slots. The accumulator was a
416	    // CSA_MAX_D_MODEL (=64) per-thread register array that pinned register
417	    // pressure (and spilled to local on real ptxas); moving it into this
418	    // thread's private shared slot is BIT-IDENTICAL — the same float adds in
419	    // the same order, only the storage class changes (register/local -> smem).
420	    extern __shared__ float csa_qsh[];
421	    if (gid >= total) return;
422	    const int t = gid / num_heads;
423	    const int h = gid % num_heads;
424	    const int hoff = h * head_dim;
425	
426	    const float scale = rsqrtf(static_cast<float>(head_dim));
427	
428	    float* acc = csa_qsh + (blockDim.x + threadIdx.x) * head_dim;  // private slot
429	    #pragma unroll
430	    for (int e = 0; e < head_dim; e++) acc[e] = 0.0f;
431	    float run_max = -INFINITY, run_denom = 0.0f;
432	
433	    // Background-load this thread's reused query slice into shared via cp.async.
434	    const float* qv = csa_stage_query_async(
435	        csa_qsh, q + t * d_model + hoff, head_dim);
436	
437	    // Selected compressed entries.
438	    for (int i = 0; i < topk; i++) {
439	        const int s = sel_idx[t * topk + i];
440	        if (s < 0 || s >= Nc) continue;
441	        alg::sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate(
442	            qv, c_k + s * d_model + hoff, c_v + s * d_model + hoff,
443	            &run_max, &run_denom, acc, scale, head_dim);
444	    }
445	    // Causal sliding window over raw tokens [t-csa_window+1 .. t].
446	    const int w0 = (t - csa_window + 1 > 0) ? (t - csa_window + 1) : 0;
447	    for (int s = w0; s <= t; s++) {
448	        alg::sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate(
449	            qv, win_k + s * d_model + hoff, win_v + s * d_model + hoff,
450	            &run_max, &run_denom, acc, scale, head_dim);
451	    }
452	    alg::sg2_softmax_finalize(acc, run_denom, head_dim);
453	
454	    // Out projection (this head's slice contributes to all output channels).
455	    // We write the head-local attention output back into a temporary head slot
456	    // of csa_ctx, then a second pass applies out_W. To keep one kernel, we
457	    // fold out_W here per output channel d that this head owns is insufficient;
458	    // instead store the concatenated heads then project. Store head slice:
459	    for (int e = 0; e < head_dim; e++)
460	        csa_ctx[t * d_model + hoff + e] = acc[e];
461	    (void)out_W;  // applied by attn_out_proj_kernel after head concatenation
462	}
463	
464	// ── (3') Output projection applied after attention (concat heads -> out_W) ─
465	__global__ void attn_out_proj_kernel(
466	    const float* __restrict__ attn_concat,   // [N, d_model] concatenated heads
467	    const float* __restrict__ out_W,         // [d_model, d_model]
468	    float* __restrict__ ctx_out,             // [N, d_model]
469	    int N, int d_model
470	) {
471	    const int total = N * d_model;
472	    const int stride = gridDim.x * blockDim.x;
473	    for (int idx = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; idx < total; idx += stride) {
474	        const int t = idx / d_model;
475	        const int d = idx % d_model;
476	        float acc = 0.0f;
477	        #pragma unroll 4
478	        for (int k = 0; k < d_model; k++)
479	            acc += out_W[d * d_model + k] * attn_concat[t * d_model + k];
480	        ctx_out[idx] = acc;
481	    }
482	}

484	// ── (4) HCA attention ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
485	//  Per query t and head h: dense online-softmax attention over ALL Nh
486	//  compressed entries ∪ the causal sliding window. No top-k selection.
487	//  Output stored as concatenated heads (project with attn_out_proj_kernel).
488	
489	__global__ void hca_attention_kernel(
490	    const float* __restrict__ q,             // [N, d_model] projected queries
491	    const float* __restrict__ c_k,           // [Nh, d_model] compressed keys
492	    const float* __restrict__ c_v,           // [Nh, d_model] compressed values
493	    const float* __restrict__ win_k,         // [N, d_model]
494	    const float* __restrict__ win_v,         // [N, d_model]
495	    float* __restrict__ hca_concat,          // [N, d_model] output (concat heads)
496	    int N, int Nh, int d_model, int num_heads,
497	    int head_dim, int csa_window
498	) {
499	    const int gid = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
500	    const int total = N * num_heads;
501	    // §4.2 query staging buffer + SMEM-staged online-softmax accumulator (same
502	    // layout/argument as csa_attention_kernel; bit-identical relocation of the
503	    // CSA_MAX_D_MODEL per-thread acc[] register array into this thread's private
504	    // shared slot).
505	    extern __shared__ float hca_qsh[];
506	    if (gid >= total) return;
507	    const int t = gid / num_heads;
508	    const int h = gid % num_heads;
509	    const int hoff = h * head_dim;
510	
511	    const float scale = rsqrtf(static_cast<float>(head_dim));
512	
513	    float* acc = hca_qsh + (blockDim.x + threadIdx.x) * head_dim;  // private slot
514	    #pragma unroll
515	    for (int e = 0; e < head_dim; e++) acc[e] = 0.0f;
516	    float run_max = -INFINITY, run_denom = 0.0f;
517	
518	    // Background-load this thread's reused query slice into shared via cp.async.
519	    const float* qv = csa_stage_query_async(
520	        hca_qsh, q + t * d_model + hoff, head_dim);
521	
522	    for (int s = 0; s < Nh; s++) {
523	        alg::sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate(
524	            qv, c_k + s * d_model + hoff, c_v + s * d_model + hoff,
525	            &run_max, &run_denom, acc, scale, head_dim);
526	    }
527	    const int w0 = (t - csa_window + 1 > 0) ? (t - csa_window + 1) : 0;
528	    for (int s = w0; s <= t; s++) {
529	        alg::sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate(
530	            qv, win_k + s * d_model + hoff, win_v + s * d_model + hoff,
531	            &run_max, &run_denom, acc, scale, head_dim);
532	    }
533	    alg::sg2_softmax_finalize(acc, run_denom, head_dim);
534	
535	    for (int e = 0; e < head_dim; e++)
536	        hca_concat[t * d_model + hoff + e] = acc[e];
537	}

546	// One thread per d_inner dimension, sequential over timesteps.
547	
548	template <typename ActT>
549	__global__ void __launch_bounds__(128, 4)
550	sequential_scan_kernel(
551	    const ActT* __restrict__ x,       // [B, N, d_inner]
552	    const ActT* __restrict__ dt,      // [B, N, d_inner]
553	    const ActT* __restrict__ A_log,   // [d_inner, d_state]

558	    int seq_len, int d_inner, int d_state

568	    #pragma unroll 4
569	    for (int s = 0; s < d_state; s++)

598	// ── Parallel Blelloch scan kernel (N >= PSCAN_THRESHOLD) ──────────────
599	// One block per (batch, d_inner). Affine2x2 prefix scan across timesteps,
600	// processing d_state pairs two at a time through the 2x2 matrix machinery.
601	
602	template <typename ActT>
603	__global__ void __launch_bounds__(256, 2)
604	parallel_scan_kernel(
605	    const ActT* __restrict__ x,
606	    const ActT* __restrict__ dt,
607	    const ActT* __restrict__ A_log,
608	    const ActT* __restrict__ B,
609	    const ActT* __restrict__ C,
610	    ActT* __restrict__ y,
611	    float* __restrict__ state_save,
612	    int seq_len, int d_inner, int d_state
613	) {
614	    const int b = blockIdx.y;
615	    const int j = blockIdx.x;
616	    if (j >= d_inner) return;
617	    const int ltid = threadIdx.x;
618	    const int nthreads = blockDim.x;
619	    const int N = seq_len;
620	    const int bN = b * N;
621	    const int bDi = b * d_inner;
622	
623	    extern __shared__ float smem[];  // 6 * nthreads
624	
625	    const int chunk = (N + nthreads - 1) / nthreads;
626	    const int t0 = ltid * chunk;
627	    const int t1 = min(t0 + chunk, N);
628	    const int cnt = max(t1 - t0, 0);
629	
630	    float A_coeff[MAX_D_STATE];
631	    #pragma unroll 4
632	    for (int s = 0; s < d_state; s++)
633	        A_coeff[s] = -ptx_expf(static_cast<float>(A_log[j * d_state + s]));
634	
635	    // Zero output for accumulation across d_state pairs
636	    for (int step = 0; step < cnt; step++) {
637	        y[(bN + t0 + step) * d_inner + j] = static_cast<ActT>(0.0f);
638	    }
639	    __syncthreads();
640	
641	    const int half_ds = d_state / 2;
642	
643	    for (int p = 0; p < half_ds; p++) {
644	        const int s0 = 2 * p, s1 = 2 * p + 1;
645	
646	        // Phase 1: sequential scan within chunk -> summary Affine2x2
647	        Affine2x2 summary = affine_identity();
648	        #pragma unroll 4
649	        for (int step = 0; step < cnt; step++) {
650	            int t = t0 + step;
651	            float dtv = static_cast<float>(dt[(bN + t) * d_inner + j]);
652	            float xv  = static_cast<float>(x[(bN + t) * d_inner + j]);
653	            Affine2x2 elem;
654	            elem.m00 = ptx_expf(A_coeff[s0] * dtv);  elem.m01 = 0.0f;
655	            elem.m10 = 0.0f;                          elem.m11 = ptx_expf(A_coeff[s1] * dtv);
656	            elem.b0  = dtv * static_cast<float>(B[(bN + t) * d_state + s0]) * xv;
657	            elem.b1  = dtv * static_cast<float>(B[(bN + t) * d_state + s1]) * xv;
658	            summary = affine_combine(summary, elem);
659	        }
660	
661	        int base = ltid * 6;
662	        smem[base]   = summary.m00; smem[base+1] = summary.m01;
663	        smem[base+2] = summary.m10; smem[base+3] = summary.m11;
664	        smem[base+4] = summary.b0;  smem[base+5] = summary.b1;
665	        __syncthreads();
666	
667	        // Phase 2: Blelloch up-sweep
668	        for (int stride = 1; stride < nthreads; stride *= 2) {
669	            int idx = (ltid + 1) * stride * 2 - 1;
670	            if (idx < nthreads) {
671	                Affine2x2 L = {smem[(idx-stride)*6],   smem[(idx-stride)*6+1],
672	                               smem[(idx-stride)*6+2], smem[(idx-stride)*6+3],
673	                               smem[(idx-stride)*6+4], smem[(idx-stride)*6+5]};
674	                Affine2x2 R = {smem[idx*6],   smem[idx*6+1],
675	                               smem[idx*6+2], smem[idx*6+3],
676	                               smem[idx*6+4], smem[idx*6+5]};
677	                Affine2x2 c = affine_combine(L, R);
678	                smem[idx*6]=c.m00; smem[idx*6+1]=c.m01; smem[idx*6+2]=c.m10;
679	                smem[idx*6+3]=c.m11; smem[idx*6+4]=c.b0; smem[idx*6+5]=c.b1;
680	            }
681	            if (stride * 2 >= WARP_SIZE) __syncthreads();
682	            else __syncwarp();
683	        }
684	
685	        // Set last to identity (exclusive scan)
686	        if (ltid == 0) {
687	            int last = (nthreads - 1) * 6;
688	            smem[last]=1; smem[last+1]=0; smem[last+2]=0;
689	            smem[last+3]=1; smem[last+4]=0; smem[last+5]=0;
690	        }
691	        __syncthreads();
692	
693	        // Down-sweep
694	        for (int stride = nthreads / 2; stride >= 1; stride /= 2) {
695	            int idx = (ltid + 1) * stride * 2 - 1;
696	            if (idx < nthreads) {
697	                Affine2x2 L = {smem[(idx-stride)*6],   smem[(idx-stride)*6+1],
698	                               smem[(idx-stride)*6+2], smem[(idx-stride)*6+3],
699	                               smem[(idx-stride)*6+4], smem[(idx-stride)*6+5]};
700	                Affine2x2 R = {smem[idx*6],   smem[idx*6+1],
701	                               smem[idx*6+2], smem[idx*6+3],
702	                               smem[idx*6+4], smem[idx*6+5]};
703	                smem[(idx-stride)*6]=R.m00; smem[(idx-stride)*6+1]=R.m01;
704	                smem[(idx-stride)*6+2]=R.m10; smem[(idx-stride)*6+3]=R.m11;
705	                smem[(idx-stride)*6+4]=R.b0; smem[(idx-stride)*6+5]=R.b1;
706	                Affine2x2 c = affine_combine(R, L);
707	                smem[idx*6]=c.m00; smem[idx*6+1]=c.m01; smem[idx*6+2]=c.m10;
708	                smem[idx*6+3]=c.m11; smem[idx*6+4]=c.b0; smem[idx*6+5]=c.b1;
709	            }
710	            if (stride * 2 >= WARP_SIZE) __syncthreads();
711	            else __syncwarp();
712	        }
713	
714	        // Phase 3: re-scan with prefix, accumulate output
715	        Affine2x2 run = {smem[ltid*6], smem[ltid*6+1], smem[ltid*6+2],
716	                         smem[ltid*6+3], smem[ltid*6+4], smem[ltid*6+5]};
717	        #pragma unroll 4
718	        for (int step = 0; step < cnt; step++) {
719	            int t = t0 + step;
720	            float dtv = static_cast<float>(dt[(bN + t) * d_inner + j]);
721	            float xv  = static_cast<float>(x[(bN + t) * d_inner + j]);
722	            Affine2x2 elem;
723	            elem.m00 = ptx_expf(A_coeff[s0] * dtv);  elem.m01 = 0.0f;
724	            elem.m10 = 0.0f;                          elem.m11 = ptx_expf(A_coeff[s1] * dtv);
725	            elem.b0  = dtv * static_cast<float>(B[(bN + t) * d_state + s0]) * xv;
726	            elem.b1  = dtv * static_cast<float>(B[(bN + t) * d_state + s1]) * xv;
727	            run = affine_combine(run, elem);
728	
729	            // h = run applied to zero initial state -> h = run.b
730	            float c0 = static_cast<float>(C[(bN + t) * d_state + s0]);
731	            float c1 = static_cast<float>(C[(bN + t) * d_state + s1]);
732	            float prev = static_cast<float>(y[(bN + t) * d_inner + j]);
733	            y[(bN + t) * d_inner + j] = static_cast<ActT>(prev + run.b0*c0 + run.b1*c1);
734	        }
735	
736	        if (state_save != nullptr && t1 == N && cnt > 0) {
737	            state_save[(bDi + j) * d_state + s0] = run.b0;
738	            state_save[(bDi + j) * d_state + s1] = run.b1;
739	        }
740	        __syncthreads();
741	    }
742	
743	    // Handle odd d_state
744	    if (d_state % 2 != 0) {
745	        const int s = d_state - 1;
746	        float hv = 0.0f;
747	        for (int step = 0; step < cnt; step++) {
748	            int t = t0 + step;
749	            float dtv = static_cast<float>(dt[(bN + t) * d_inner + j]);
750	            float xv  = static_cast<float>(x[(bN + t) * d_inner + j]);
751	            hv = ptx_expf(A_coeff[s] * dtv) * hv
752	               + dtv * static_cast<float>(B[(bN + t) * d_state + s]) * xv;
753	            float prev = static_cast<float>(y[(bN + t) * d_inner + j]);
754	            float cv   = static_cast<float>(C[(bN + t) * d_state + s]);
755	            y[(bN + t) * d_inner + j] = static_cast<ActT>(prev + hv * cv);
756	        }
757	        if (state_save != nullptr && t1 == N && cnt > 0)
758	            state_save[(bDi + j) * d_state + s] = hv;
759	    }
760	}
761	
762	// ── Forward dispatch ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
763	
764	template <typename ActT>
765	cudaError_t selective_scan_forward(
766	    const ActT* x, const ActT* dt, const ActT* A_log,
767	    const ActT* B, const ActT* C,
768	    ActT* y, float* state_save,
769	    int batch, int seq_len, int d_inner, int d_state,
770	    cudaStream_t stream
771	) {
772	    if (seq_len < PSCAN_THRESHOLD) {
773	        int block = min(d_inner, 128);
774	        dim3 grid((d_inner + block - 1) / block, batch);
775	        sequential_scan_kernel<ActT><<<grid, block, 0, stream>>>(
776	            x, dt, A_log, B, C, y, state_save, seq_len, d_inner, d_state);
777	    } else {
778	        int block = min(PSCAN_BLOCK, 256);
779	        dim3 grid(d_inner, batch);
780	        int smem_bytes = 6 * block * sizeof(float);
781	        parallel_scan_kernel<ActT><<<grid, block, smem_bytes, stream>>>(
782	            x, dt, A_log, B, C, y, state_save, seq_len, d_inner, d_state);
783	    }
784	    return cudaGetLastError();
785	}
786	
787	// ── Backward: adjoint scan ────────────────────────────────────────────
788	// Reverse-time sequential scan computing gradients through the recurrence.
789	// For each timestep t (in reverse):
790	//   grad_h += C[t] * grad_y[t]
791	//   grad_B[t] = dt[t] * x[t] * grad_h
792	//   grad_C[t] = h[t] * grad_y[t]   (h[t] recomputed via forward pass)
793	//   grad_x[t] = sum_s(B[t,s] * dt[t] * grad_h[s])
794	//   grad_dt[t] = sum_s(A[s]*A_bar*h[t-1,s] + B[t,s]*x[t]) * grad_h[s]
795	//   grad_A_log[j,s] += dt[t]*A[s]*A_bar * h[t-1,s] * grad_h[s]
796	//   grad_h = A_bar * grad_h   (backprop through recurrence)
797	
798	template <typename ActT>
799	__global__ void __launch_bounds__(128, 4)
800	scan_backward_kernel(
801	    const ActT* __restrict__ grad_y,
802	    const ActT* __restrict__ x,
803	    const ActT* __restrict__ dt,
804	    const ActT* __restrict__ A_log,
805	    const ActT* __restrict__ B,
806	    const ActT* __restrict__ C,
807	    const float* __restrict__ state_save,
808	    ActT* __restrict__ grad_x,
809	    ActT* __restrict__ grad_dt,
810	    float* __restrict__ grad_A_log,  // [d_inner, d_state], atomicAdd
811	    ActT* __restrict__ grad_B,
812	    ActT* __restrict__ grad_C,
813	    int seq_len, int d_inner, int d_state
814	) {
815	    const int b = blockIdx.y;
816	    const int j = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
817	    if (j >= d_inner) return;
818	
819	    const int bN  = b * seq_len;
820	    const int bDi = b * d_inner;
821	
822	    float A[MAX_D_STATE];
823	    #pragma unroll 4
824	    for (int s = 0; s < d_state; s++)
825	        A[s] = -ptx_expf(static_cast<float>(A_log[j * d_state + s]));
826	
827	    // Forward pass to cache h[t] for all t (needed for grad_C and grad_dt)
828	    float h_cache[MAX_D_STATE];
829	    float h_prev[MAX_D_STATE];
830	    #pragma unroll 4
831	    for (int s = 0; s < d_state; s++) h_cache[s] = 0.0f;
832	
833	    // Allocate per-timestep h cache in local memory (seq_len is small)
834	    float h_all[256 * MAX_D_STATE];  // PSCAN_THRESHOLD * MAX_D_STATE
835	
836	    // Forward recompute
837	    for (int t = 0; t < seq_len; t++) {
838	        float xv  = static_cast<float>(x[(bN + t) * d_inner + j]);
839	        float dtv = static_cast<float>(dt[(bN + t) * d_inner + j]);
840	        #pragma unroll 4
841	        for (int s = 0; s < d_state; s++) {
842	            float A_bar = ptx_expf(A[s] * dtv);
843	            float B_bar = dtv * static_cast<float>(B[(bN + t) * d_state + s]);
844	            h_cache[s] = A_bar * h_cache[s] + B_bar * xv;
845	            h_all[t * d_state + s] = h_cache[s];
846	        }
847	    }
848	
849	    // Reverse pass for gradients
850	    float grad_h[MAX_D_STATE];
851	    float grad_A_acc[MAX_D_STATE];
852	    #pragma unroll 4
853	    for (int s = 0; s < d_state; s++) { grad_h[s] = 0.0f; grad_A_acc[s] = 0.0f; }
854	
855	    for (int t = seq_len - 1; t >= 0; t--) {
856	        float xv   = static_cast<float>(x[(bN + t) * d_inner + j]);
857	        float dtv  = static_cast<float>(dt[(bN + t) * d_inner + j]);
858	        float gy   = static_cast<float>(grad_y[(bN + t) * d_inner + j]);
859	
860	        float grad_x_acc  = 0.0f;
861	        float grad_dt_acc = 0.0f;
862	
863	        #pragma unroll 4
864	        for (int s = 0; s < d_state; s++) {
865	            float A_bar = ptx_expf(A[s] * dtv);
866	            float bv    = static_cast<float>(B[(bN + t) * d_state + s]);
867	            float cv    = static_cast<float>(C[(bN + t) * d_state + s]);
868	            float h_t   = h_all[t * d_state + s];
869	            float h_tm1 = (t > 0) ? h_all[(t-1) * d_state + s] : 0.0f;
870	
871	            // grad_C[t,s] = h[t,s] * grad_y[t]
872	            grad_C[(bN + t) * d_state + s] = static_cast<ActT>(h_t * gy);
873	
874	            // Accumulate into grad_h
875	            grad_h[s] += cv * gy;
876	
877	            // grad_B[t,s] = dt * x * grad_h[s]
878	            grad_B[(bN + t) * d_state + s] = static_cast<ActT>(dtv * xv * grad_h[s]);
879	
880	            // grad_x accumulation
881	            grad_x_acc += bv * dtv * grad_h[s];
882	
883	            // grad_dt accumulation
884	            grad_dt_acc += (A[s] * A_bar * h_tm1 + bv * xv) * grad_h[s];
885	
886	            // grad_A_log accumulation
887	            grad_A_acc[s] += dtv * A[s] * A_bar * h_tm1 * grad_h[s];
888	
889	            // Backprop through recurrence
890	            grad_h[s] = A_bar * grad_h[s];
891	        }
892	
893	        grad_x[(bN + t) * d_inner + j]  = static_cast<ActT>(grad_x_acc);
894	        grad_dt[(bN + t) * d_inner + j] = static_cast<ActT>(grad_dt_acc);
895	    }
896	
897	    // Accumulate grad_A_log across batch via atomicAdd
898	    #pragma unroll 4
899	    for (int s = 0; s < d_state; s++)
900	        atomicAdd(&grad_A_log[j * d_state + s], grad_A_acc[s]);
901	}
902	
903	// ── Backward dispatch ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
904	
905	template <typename ActT>
906	cudaError_t selective_scan_backward(
907	    const ActT* grad_y,
908	    const ActT* x, const ActT* dt, const ActT* A_log,
909	    const ActT* B, const ActT* C,
910	    const float* state_save,
911	    ActT* grad_x, ActT* grad_dt, float* grad_A_log,
912	    ActT* grad_B, ActT* grad_C,
913	    int batch, int seq_len, int d_inner, int d_state,
914	    cudaStream_t stream
915	) {
916	    cudaMemsetAsync(grad_A_log, 0, d_inner * d_state * sizeof(float), stream);
917	    int block = min(d_inner, 128);
918	    dim3 grid((d_inner + block - 1) / block, batch);
919	    scan_backward_kernel<ActT><<<grid, block, 0, stream>>>(
920	        grad_y, x, dt, A_log, B, C, state_save,
921	        grad_x, grad_dt, grad_A_log, grad_B, grad_C,
922	        seq_len, d_inner, d_state);
923	    return cudaGetLastError();
924	}

2	// csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh
3	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4	// Stage 6 — sm_90 L3 persistent-megakernel internals (§1.1–§1.4, §1.13, §1.14).
5	//
6	// This header is the **uniform scheduler + barrier substrate** that every
7	// generated L3 megakernel (csrc/fused/sm_90/*.cu) composes on top of the §3.4
8	// warp-specialization primitives (csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/warp_specialize.cuh).
9	// It defines ONLY the cross-CTA coordination machinery; the per-(model,
10	// optimizer) compute stages live in the generated TUs.
11	//
12	// The four pieces, all sm_90-real (compile-verified via
13	// scripts/compile_to_object.sh) and degrading to a correct fallback on older
14	// arches so the codegen matrix still builds:
15	//
16	//   §1.1  TaskQueue        — a single global atomic work counter that every
17	//                            persistent CTA pulls parameter-tensor indices
18	//                            from (the ThunderKittens-interpreter pattern).
19	//   §1.2  work-stealing     — there is NO static partition: an idle CTA simply
20	//                            keeps calling TaskQueue::next(), so a CTA that
21	//                            finishes its tensor early steals the next one.
22	//                            (atomicAdd on the shared counter IS the steal.)
23	//   §1.3  sm_id()           — reads %smid so the host can pin one persistent
24	//                            CTA per SM and keep that SM's optimizer-state
25	//                            slice L2-warm across the step.
26	//   §1.4  GridBarrier       — a hand-built arrive/wait grid barrier from two
27	//                            global atomics + a sense-reversing generation
28	//                            counter. Reusable, needs NO cooperative launch
29	//                            (so it scales past the cooperative-grid CTA cap).
30	//
31	// §1.14 fences: acquire/release are placed EXPLICITLY and MINIMALLY — exactly
32	// one __threadfence() before the arrival publish and one acquire load after
33	// the release wait at the barrier, and one fence at the task hand-off. No loose
34	// fences (a loose fence here is both a correctness and a >10% perf footgun).
35	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
36	
37	#include "csrc/common/platform.h"
38	#include "csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/warp_specialize.cuh"
39	#include <cuda_runtime.h>
40	
41	namespace sg { namespace fused {
42	
43	// =========================================================================
44	//  §1.3  SM-pinning: read the streaming-multiprocessor id via %smid.
45	//
46	//  The host launches exactly gridDim.x == #SMs CTAs (one persistent CTA per
47	//  SM) and uses sm_id() inside the kernel to index that SM's resident slice
48	//  of optimizer state, so the slice stays warm in this SM's L2 partition for
49	//  the whole step. On pre-sm_90 the asm is still valid (%smid exists since
50	//  sm_20); the guard only exists to keep a host-compile of this header clean.
51	// =========================================================================
52	__device__ __forceinline__ unsigned sm_id() {
53	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__)
54	    unsigned id;
55	    asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%smid;" : "=r"(id));
56	    return id;
57	#else
58	    return 0u;
59	#endif
60	}
61	
62	// =========================================================================
63	//  §1.1 / §1.2  TaskQueue — global work counter + work-stealing.
64	//
65	//  One int in global memory (`g_next_task`, zero-initialized by the host).
66	//  Every CTA runs:
67	//      for (int t = q.next(); t < n_tasks; t = q.next()) process(t);
68	//  next() does `atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1)` — a CTA that drains its tensor
69	//  early just grabs the next index, so faster SMs steal work from the queue
70	//  with no static load-balancing (§1.2). The atomic is the ONLY synchronizer;
71	//  task bodies are independent (one parameter tensor each), so no fence is
72	//  needed on the *pull* — the fence belongs at the grid barrier between the
73	//  forward / backward / optimizer phases (§1.4), not on the per-task pull.
74	//
75	//  By convention ONE thread per CTA (the elected leader) pulls a task and
76	//  broadcasts it to the block via shared memory; `next_block()` packages that.
77	// =========================================================================
78	struct TaskQueue {
79	    int* g_next_task;   // global counter (host memset to 0 before launch)
80	    int  n_tasks;       // total parameter tensors to process this phase
81	
82	    __device__ __forceinline__ explicit TaskQueue(int* counter, int total)
83	        : g_next_task(counter), n_tasks(total) {}
84	
85	    // Per-thread atomic pull (used when every thread independently claims work,
86	    // e.g. a warp-granular schedule). Returns a task index that may be >=
87	    // n_tasks (caller bounds-checks).
88	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next() {
89	        return atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
90	    }
91	
92	    // Per-CTA pull: the leader thread does the single atomicAdd and broadcasts
93	    // the claimed index to the whole block through `smem_slot`. All threads in
94	    // the block then cooperate on that one tensor. Returns the claimed index.
95	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next_block(int* smem_slot) {
96	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
97	            *smem_slot = atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
98	        }
99	        __syncthreads();
100	        int t = *smem_slot;
101	        __syncthreads();   // ensure every thread read before slot is reused
102	        return t;
103	    }
104	};
105	
106	// =========================================================================
107	//  §1.4  GridBarrier — hand-built, reusable, sense-reversing grid barrier.
108	//
109	//  State (all in global memory, host-zero-initialized):
110	//    arrived    — count of CTAs that have reached the current barrier
111	//    generation — flips/advances each time the barrier is crossed (the "sense"
112	//                 a late CTA waits on so an early CTA can't lap it)
113	//
114	//  The classic correctness hazard with a counter barrier is *reuse*: if you
115	//  just reset `arrived` to 0, a fast CTA can enter the NEXT barrier and
116	//  increment the counter before a slow CTA has observed the release of the
117	//  PREVIOUS one. The sense-reversing generation fixes this: each CTA samples
118	//  the generation on entry, then waits until the generation has ADVANCED
119	//  (the last arriver advances it), never touching `arrived` for reset on the
120	//  consumer side. The last CTA to arrive resets `arrived` to 0 and bumps the
121	//  generation in one release; everyone else spins on the generation.
122	//
123	//  Fences (§1.14):
124	//    * The releasing writes a CTA makes BEFORE the barrier (its phase output)
125	//      must be visible to peers AFTER the barrier. We publish arrival with a
126	//      __threadfence() (device-scope release) before the atomicAdd, and the
127	//      waiters do an acquire by reading the generation with volatile semantics
128	//      and a __threadfence() after the wait completes. Exactly two fences per
129	//      CTA per barrier — the minimum for a correct release/acquire pair.
130	//
131	//  Only thread 0 of each CTA participates in the cross-CTA handshake; the rest
132	//  of the block is gated by a __syncthreads() so the whole CTA leaves together.
133	// =========================================================================
134	struct GridBarrier {
135	    unsigned* g_arrived;      // CTAs arrived at current phase
136	    unsigned* g_generation;   // sense-reversing generation counter
137	    unsigned  n_ctas;         // gridDim.x (CTAs that must arrive)
138	
139	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier(unsigned* arrived,
140	                                            unsigned* generation,
141	                                            unsigned grid_ctas)
142	        : g_arrived(arrived), g_generation(generation), n_ctas(grid_ctas) {}
143	
144	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync() const {
145	        // The block must fully reach the barrier before its leader publishes.
146	        __syncthreads();
147	
148	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
149	            // Sample the sense we are waiting to leave.
150	            unsigned my_gen =
151	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
152	
153	            // §1.14 RELEASE: make this CTA's phase writes visible device-wide
154	            // BEFORE we announce arrival, so a peer that observes our arrival
155	            // (and crosses) also observes our outputs.
156	            __threadfence();
157	
158	            // Atomically join the arrival count. The CTA whose add completes
159	            // the set (== n_ctas) is the "last arriver".
160	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
161	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
162	                // Last arriver: clear the count for the NEXT phase, then bump
163	                // the generation. Order matters — reset arrived to 0 first,
164	                // then a release-store of the advanced generation so a CTA that
165	                // sees the new generation also sees arrived==0 when it next
166	                // enters. atomicExch gives the store device-scope visibility.
167	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
168	                __threadfence();
169	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
170	            } else {
171	                // Not last: spin until the generation advances past our sample.
172	                // §1.14b BACKOFF: a tight volatile-read spin hammers the L2 /
173	                // memory subsystem with the generation poll and steals issue
174	                // slots from arriving CTAs. __nanosleep parks the spinning warp
175	                // for an exponentially-growing nap (capped) so the poll rate
176	                // drops and the memory subsystem is left to the laggard CTAs.
177	                // Behavior-preserving: still exits the instant the generation
178	                // advances; only the *poll cadence* changes (sm_70+; on older
179	                // arches the asm is a no-op fallback).
180	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
181	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
182	                       == my_gen) {
183	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
184	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
185	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
186	#endif
187	                }
188	            }
189	
190	            // §1.14 ACQUIRE: after observing the generation advance, fence so
191	            // the peers' phase writes (released above) are visible to us.
192	            __threadfence();
193	        }
194	
195	        // Release the rest of the block once the leader has crossed.
196	        __syncthreads();
197	    }
198	
199	    // #4 — barrier with a FUSED task-counter reset. The L3 phase loop used to do
200	    //   fwd → sync → reset_counter → sync → bwd → sync → reset_counter → sync
201	    // (4 grid barriers + 2 standalone in-kernel counter resets). The reset is
202	    // folded into THIS barrier's last-arriver critical section: the last CTA
203	    // zeroes `*reset_counter` BEFORE the release-store that advances the
204	    // generation, so any CTA that later observes the new generation (and thus
205	    // crosses) is guaranteed to see the counter == 0 for the next phase. That
206	    // removes the two standalone resets AND their two barriers — 4 → 2 grid
207	    // barriers per L3 step — with identical phase ordering/visibility. Pass the
208	    // task-queue counter (ctx.g_next_task) as `reset_counter`.
209	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync_reset(int* reset_counter) const {
210	        __syncthreads();
211	
212	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
213	            unsigned my_gen =
214	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
215	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 RELEASE: publish phase writes before arrival.
216	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
217	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
218	                // Last arriver: clear arrival count AND reset the task counter
219	                // for the next phase, then a release-store of the advanced
220	                // generation. Ordering: both resets, then __threadfence(), then
221	                // the generation bump — so observers of the new gen see both
222	                // arrived==0 and reset_counter==0.
223	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
224	                atomicExch(reinterpret_cast<unsigned*>(reset_counter), 0u);
225	                __threadfence();
226	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
227	            } else {
228	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
229	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
230	                       == my_gen) {
231	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
232	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
233	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
234	#endif
235	                }
236	            }
237	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 ACQUIRE.
238	        }
239	
240	        __syncthreads();
241	    }
242	};
243	
244	// =========================================================================
245	//  PersistentContext — the bundle of global scratch a generated L3 megakernel
246	//  needs. The host allocates these (all zero-initialized) and passes their
247	//  device pointers to the kernel. Grouping them keeps the generated kernel
248	//  signatures uniform across all 99 cells.
249	// =========================================================================
250	struct PersistentContext {
251	    int*      g_next_task;     // §1.1 TaskQueue counter
252	    unsigned* g_arrived;       // §1.4 GridBarrier arrival count
253	    unsigned* g_generation;    // §1.4 GridBarrier generation
254	    int       n_tasks;         // parameter tensors this step
255	    unsigned  n_ctas;          // persistent CTAs (== #SMs, one per SM, §1.3)
256	
257	    __device__ __forceinline__ TaskQueue queue() const {
258	        return TaskQueue(g_next_task, n_tasks);
259	    }
260	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier barrier() const {
261	        return GridBarrier(g_arrived, g_generation, n_ctas);
262	    }
263	};

40	// 2-3x faster than sqrtf(x) + fdividef for Adam denominator.
41	__device__ __forceinline__ float fast_rsqrt_nr(float x) {

98	// Compile-time maximums (must match types.h constants).
99	constexpr int SG2_MAX_D_MODEL = 64;     // upper bound on per-element feature width
100	
101	// ── CSA/HCA compressed-attention maximums (spec §2, §3) ──
102	// These bound per-thread register arrays used by the device helpers below.
103	constexpr int SG2_CSA_WINDOW_MAX  = 16;   // max sliding-window / KV-pool width (CSA_WINDOW=8 default)
104	constexpr int SG2_CSA_TOPK_MAX    = 64;   // max top-k compressed entries per query (CSA_TOPK=16 default)
105	constexpr int SG2_INDEXER_RANK_MAX = 8;   // max lightning-indexer low rank (INDEXER_RANK=4 default)
106	constexpr int SG2_HCA_COMPRESS    = 128;  // heavily-compressed pooling stride m' (spec §2 HCA)
